rationale: Evidence from iteration 7 (score 216.4, best so far): narrowing wheel_track from 0.14 to 0.11 m lifted oval completions from 5 to 6 of 20, cut oval max_error from 0.059 to 0.054 m, and lowered oval oscillation from 0.307 to 0.262. Slalom is still the weakest track, at 0.07 progress, and its line-loss events rose from 0.05 to 0.9. Line loss happens only when every sensor reads below 0.05, which needs the robot centre to move about 0.07 m or more off the tape. The current sensor row spans only ±0.06 m, so on slalom excursions the whole array can leave the tape. Change: widen the sensor row to x = -0.08, -0.04, 0, 0.04, 0.08 m, keeping the same weights, y = 0.03 m, 16 mm sensors and all controller values. Widening the spread keeps the tape under a sensor at larger offsets, and the same weights mean the signal is a little larger per unit offset, a modest gain increase. This is a single-variable change, so the slalom line-loss and progress change can be read cleanly. Expected result: slalom line_loss_events fall well below 0.9 and slalom progress rises above 0.1, while oval completions hold near 6 of 20. Hypotheses for the next race: (H1) if slalom line-loss stays near 0.9 with the wider row, the excursion is from steering lag, not sensor coverage, so kp should rise to about 5.0 with kd at 0.9. (H2) If oval oscillation rises above 0.35 from the larger signal, the spread is adding gain and the outer weights should drop to ±0.75. (H3) If all tracks survive but none finish, base_speed should move to about 1.2. Measurements wanted per track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort and noise_robustness.
